definitions: A standardized steel intermodal box of considerable length and girth, engineered to withstand ocean transit, decades of stacking, and the occasional forklift's poor judgment.
colloq. The corrugated linebacker of the shipping yard, broad enough to make a freight train reconsider its life choices.
example: The thiccc shipping container sat stacked six high at the port, blotting out the sun for anyone shorter than a crane operator.
etymology: From Latin 'contineo,' to hold together, and 'ship,' from Old English 'scip.' The forty-foot standard arrived in 1956, when Malcom McLean decided cargo deserved a proper girth.
caption: Plate CXVIII., A corrugated titan awaiting its next ocean crossing.
